title: Adjective + preposition 1
subtitle: nice of you / angry with me / tired of waiting
summary: Learn which preposition follows adjectives like nice, angry, pleased, surprised, fed up and sorry.

lesson.heading: nice of you or nice to me?
lesson.text: We use **of somebody** to say what we think of a person's action, and **to somebody** to say how a person behaves towards another person.

left.label: nice / kind / good / generous / polite / stupid / silly OF somebody (to do something)
examples: Thank you. It was very nice **of you** to help me.
It was stupid **of me** to go out without a coat in such cold weather.

right.label: (be) nice / kind / polite / rude / friendly / cruel TO somebody
examples: They have always been very nice **to me**.
Why were you so unfriendly **to Lucy**?

lesson.note: We say nice **to** me, not ~~nice with me~~.

lesson.heading: angry about something, angry with somebody
lesson.text: **angry / annoyed / furious / upset about** something, but **with somebody for doing** something.

examples.text: There's no point in getting **angry about** things that don't matter.
Are you **annoyed with** me **for** being late?
Lisa is **upset about** not being invited to the party.
Our neighbours were **furious with** us **for** making so much noise.

lesson.heading: excited about, pleased with
lesson.text: We say **excited / worried / nervous / happy about** something. But we use **with** for something you get or experience: **pleased / satisfied / happy / delighted / disappointed with**.

examples.text: Tanya doesn't look very well. I'm **worried about** her.
They were **delighted with** the present I gave them.
Were you **happy with** your exam results?

lesson.heading: surprised at/by, fed up with, tired of
lesson.text: We say **surprised / shocked / amazed / astonished / upset at** or **by** something, **impressed with** or **by** somebody, **fed up / bored with** something, and **tired of** something.

examples.text: I hope you weren't **shocked by** what I said.
I'm very **impressed with** her English. It's very good.
I don't enjoy my job any more. I'm **fed up with** it. / I'm **bored with** it.
Come on, let's go! I'm **tired of** waiting.

lesson.heading: sorry about / sorry for
lesson.text: We say **sorry about** a situation or something that happened, and **sorry for** (or about) something you did. We feel **sorry for** somebody who is in a bad situation.

examples.text: I'm **sorry about** the mess. I'll clear it up later.
I'm **sorry for** shouting at you yesterday.
I'm sorry I shouted at you yesterday.
I feel **sorry for** Mark. He's had a lot of bad luck.

lesson.text: Two to remember: we are angry **with** a person but angry **about** a thing, and we are tired **of** something we have had enough of.

exercises.prompt: Tom offered to drive me to the airport. That was nice ___ him.
exercises.explanation: We judge an action with nice/kind/stupid of somebody.

exercises.prompt: I needed money and Lisa gave me some. That was ___ her.
exercises.explanation: That was generous of her - adjective + of + person for an action.

exercises.prompt: They have always been very nice ___ me.
exercises.explanation: Be nice/kind/rude to somebody, not with somebody.

exercises.prompt: What have I done wrong? Why are you ___ me?
exercises.explanation: We are angry with a person, but angry about a thing.

exercises.prompt: You must be very ___ your trip next week. It sounds really great.
exercises.explanation: Excited, worried and nervous all take about.

exercises.prompt: Match the two halves of the sentences.

pairs.right: with the present I gave them

pairs.left: I don't enjoy my job any more. I'm fed up
Come on, let's go! I'm tired
He's had a lot of bad luck. I feel sorry

exercises.prompt: We had a good holiday, but we were disappointed ___ the hotel.
exercises.explanation: Pleased, satisfied, delighted and disappointed take with.

exercises.statement: I can't understand people who are cruel with animals.
exercises.explanation: I can't understand people who are cruel to animals. Behaviour towards somebody takes to.

exercises.prompt: I've been trying to learn Japanese, but I'm not very satisfied ___ my progress.
exercises.explanation: Satisfied with something you get or experience.

exercises.prompt: Which preposition normally follows each adjective?
There's no point in feeling sorry ___ yourself. It won't help you.
exercises.explanation: We feel sorry for a person in a bad situation.

exercises.prompt: Our neighbours were furious with us ___ making so much noise.
exercises.explanation: Furious/annoyed with somebody for doing something.
